fix_commit.message: Fix an integer overflow that could lead to a buffer overrun in the zipfile extension. Bug [bugs:/info/2026-06-01T10:16:47Z | 2026-06-01T10:16:47Z].
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: Integer overflow in zipfileBufferGrow leads to undersized allocation and buffer overrun
findings.message: The function zipfileBufferGrow() uses 32-bit int variables nNew and nReq to compute the new allocation size for the growable buffer. When pBuf->n is large (e.g., > INT_MAX/2), the expression pBuf->n*2 overflows a signed 32-bit int, yielding a negative or wrapped value for nNew. Similarly, pBuf->n+nByte in the condition check and in nReq can overflow. As a consequence, sqlite3_realloc() may be called with an insufficient (or negative, which wraps to a huge but unintended value) size, and subsequent memcpy calls write more bytes into the buffer than were allocated, resulting in a heap buffer overrun.
findings.suggestion: Use 64-bit types (i64) for nNew and nReq, cast to i64 before multiplication to avoid int overflow (e.g., (i64)pBuf->n*2), use sqlite3_realloc64 for the actual allocation, and reformulate the guard condition as (pBuf->nAlloc-pBuf->n)<nByte to avoid overflow in the sum.

ground_truth.root_cause: The function was introduced with all size variables declared as int (32-bit), without consideration that the zipfile aggregate could accumulate data larger than INT_MAX/2. The guard condition pBuf->n+nByte>pBuf->nAlloc and the growth expression pBuf->n*2 both use int arithmetic, which wraps on overflow before the value is acted upon. The use of sqlite3_realloc() (32-bit size parameter) rather than sqlite3_realloc64() compounds the issue.
